narrative: The model estimates a 67% chance that you will leave your job—about two in three—so it treats retention risk as high and denies the promotion. The strongest signal pushing toward leaving is that you have received other job opportunities while in this role; among employees predicted to stay, only about one in four had such offers. The second signal is your total experience of one to five years, which pushes toward staying; about half of employees predicted to stay are in this same early-career range. The third is your sector being “other,” which pushes toward leaving; it is less common among employees predicted to stay than medical or education. Other factors—such as feeling little job stability, lacking medical insurance, working overtime, and not feeling you received the deserved promotion—reinforce concern, though they rank below the top three. Before reconsidering, the organization should discuss your outside opportunities and internal career path, clarify promotion criteria, and address stability and benefits. You should ask what specific retention and development steps would change the decision.
